key_insight: Detonation-gun Al2O3-TiO2 coating significantly improves the tribological performance of Ti-6Al-4V, and wear can be effectively predicted from process/load parameters using machine learning.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to extend the service life of titanium alloy components in aerospace, biomedical, and marine applications where wear resistance is critical.
method: Applied ~200 µm Al2O3-TiO2 ceramic coating to Ti-6Al-4V using D-gun under controlled spray conditions.
Evaluated wear with pin-on-disc testing per ASTM G99 across 40–100 N, 100–200 rpm, and 20–40 min against EN31 steel.
Trained ANN, KNN, and random forest models to predict wear from sliding parameters.
evidence_signal: SEM and tribology results showed reduced wear and formation of a protective tribo-layer on coated samples; random forest gave the lowest mean percentage error and mean squared error among the tested models.
watch_item: The model and coating performance are based on a limited experimental parameter range, so extrapolation to other loads, speeds, or service environments should be validated.
paper_title: Tribological enhancement of Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 D-gun coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: A machine learning approach
